description:
Engineered for Explosive Power. Proven by Champions.

The Carbon Sprint Track Bars are purpose-built for one thing: maximum control and stiffness for elite track sprinters. These UCI legal bars are widely adopted by professional riders at the highest level of competition, these bars deliver the confidence, handling, and performance required to dominate the sprint events — from match sprints, team sprints and keirin.

Crafted from high-modulus carbon fibre, the Sprint Bars combine an aerodynamic profile with a radical, aggressive geometry that both reduces drag and provides a stunning visual signature. The result is a handlebar trusted by more professional sprinters worldwide than any other, making it the go-to choice for those who demand uncompromising performance.

Sprint-Specific Aerodynamics & Stiffness

Unlike endurance-focused bars, the Carbon Sprint Track Bars are designed around the unique demands of sprint racing. Every contour is shaped to reduce frontal area and channel airflow cleanly around the rider’s arms and torso, providing marginal aerodynamic gains without compromising rigidity.

The ultra-stiff carbon layup ensures direct power transfer, meaning every watt from the rider’s legs is delivered to the track with minimal loss. This stiffness not only improves acceleration out of the gate but also ensures pinpoint handling precision at maximum velocity — critical when racing shoulder-to-shoulder at over 70 km/h.

Optimised Sprint Geometry

The aggressive geometry has been refined through extensive professional use, providing the ideal balance of control, leverage, and aerodynamics:

Width Tops: 50mm x 310 mm
– Aerodynamically profiled to reduce drag

Width Drops (C-C): 350 mm
– Narrow sprint profile to reduce drag and allow tighter racing lines -
UCI LEGAL

Drop: 72 mm
– Compact but deep enough for maximum leverage and control

Reach: 90 mm
– Compact and aggressive to keep the rider locked in a forward, aero position

This geometry keeps the rider low and stable in full-flight efforts, while the compact cockpit enhances bike handling during tactical match sprints and high-speed keirin finishes.

Race-Proven by Professionals

The Carbon Sprint Track Bars are now the most popular sprint handlebar among elite riders worldwide, trusted in Olympic finals, World Championships, and Nations Cups. Their dominance in the professional peloton is testament to their blend of stiffness, control, and aerodynamic efficiency — making them the benchmark for sprint performance.
They are fully UCI legal, including the 1 January 2027 rule changes as the drops are 350mm centre to centre.

Sprint Without Limits

From explosive standing starts to final-lap drag races, the Carbon Sprint Track Bars deliver the stiffness, control, and aerodynamic advantage that elite sprinters demand. For riders chasing Olympic-level performance, these bars provide the competitive edge needed to launch, accelerate, and finish first.

Track Cycling Strength Tested

ISO 4210 is a road and racing bicycle safety standard, not a dedicated track cycling standard. Testing only to that baseline is not appropriate for the higher strength demands of elite velodrome racing, where far greater loads are placed through the handlebar.

For this reason, our handlebars are validated to a higher track-specific benchmark, targeting
180-200 N/mm stiffness
,
2500 N minimum unilateral compression strength
,
3000 N peak static proof loading
, and
500,000 fatigue cycles at 3 Hz

This gives a far stronger basis for high-load track use than a road-derived safety standard alone.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q: Are the Carbon Sprint Track Bars UCI legal?
A: Yes, these bars fully comply with UCI regulations and are approved for use in all levels of competition, including World Championships and the Olympic Games.

Q: Who are these handlebars designed for?
A: The Carbon Sprint Track Bars are optimised for sprinters and keirin riders who demand maximum stiffness, control, and aerodynamic efficiency.

Q: How do these differ from the Carbon Aero Bunch Bars?
A: The Sprint Bars feature a narrower, more aggressive geometry designed specifically for sprint events, whereas the Aero Bunch Bars offer more versatile grip positions for points, scratch, Madison, and bunch racing.

Q: What stem clamp size do they use?
A: The Carbon Sprint Track Bars use a 31.8 mm stem clamp diameter.

description:
The Carbon Aero Bunch Pro Bars take everything that makes the standard Carbon Aero Bunch Bars exceptional — and push performance to an even higher level. Designed for elite riders chasing marginal gains, the Pro Bars deliver enhanced aerodynamics, increased stiffness, and further weight optimisation in a race-ready, UCI-legal package.

Developed through advanced CFD analysis and extensive rider feedback from world-class athletes, the Pro Bars are purpose-built for riders who demand every possible advantage in high-speed bunch racing and championship-level events.

Crafted from next-generation aerospace-grade Toray carbon fibre with an ultra-high modulus resin system, the Pro Bars deliver increased lateral stiffness and an even lighter overall weight — maximising power transfer during explosive accelerations while maintaining supreme control deep into the race.

CFD-Optimized Aerodynamics — Elevated

Every aspect of the Carbon Aero Bunch Pro Bars has been refined using advanced Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) to achieve class-leading aerodynamic efficiency. Compared to traditional round-profile handlebars — and even outperforming the standard Carbon Aero Bunch Bars — the Pro version has been reshaped and tuned to shave precious watts when it matters most.

By simulating thousands of airflow scenarios in a virtual wind tunnel and validating results with on-track testing, we’ve created a handlebar that offers unrivalled aerodynamic integration between rider and bike.

Key aerodynamic upgrades include:

Up to 9% Drag Reduction
vs traditional round-profile handlebars

Enhanced CFD Shaping
– Optimised transitions across every grip position

Ultra-Narrow Frontal Area
– New refined top profile slices the air more efficiently

Optimised Pressure Zones
– Improved shaping for smoother airflow and reduced drag hotspots

Performance Validated
– Verified through real-world testing with elite-level riders

In elite bunch racing and championship Madison events, where speeds regularly exceed 50 km/h, these refinements deliver measurable power savings, lower fatigue, and a clear competitive edge.

Five Versatile Grip Positions

Like the standard Carbon Aero Bunch Bars, the Pro model offers five carefully optimised grip positions — but with subtly reshaped profiles and edges for improved ergonomics and seamless transitions:

Classic Drops
– Maximum control with a confident, responsive feel.

Forward Drops
– Lower your elbows and reduce frontal drag for maximum aero gains.

Hood-Grip
– Raised “fake hoods” position supports aerobic recovery during intense bunch racing.

– Aero-profiled flat tops redesigned with a reinforced platform for Madison slings and aggressive race manoeuvres.

Race-Optimised Geometry

With refinements to the reach and drop, the Carbon Aero Bunch Pro Bars deliver an even more aggressive aerodynamic position without sacrificing rider stability or long-duration comfort.

Fully UCI-approved for all current and forthcoming regulations, ensuring unrestricted use at the highest level of international competition.

Asymmetric Stem Clamp Design

The Carbon Aero Bunch Pro Bars feature an innovative asymmetric stem clamp position, specifically engineered to create a larger, flatter top platform — optimised for Madison slings and aggressive race manoeuvres.

By shifting the clamp interface subtly, we’ve freed up additional usable surface area on the tops without compromising stiffness, safety, or UCI compliance. The result is a more stable and controlled hand position during high-speed exchanges, giving riders the confidence and precision needed to execute smooth, efficient slings at full race pace.

This subtle but performance-driven refinement makes the Carbon Aero Bunch Pro Bars the ultimate choice for Madison specialists and elite riders looking for every marginal gain in bunch racing scenarios.

The Carbon Aero Bunch Track Handlebar redefines what a bunch bar can be — combining cutting-edge aerodynamics, precision handling, and elite-level stiffness in an ultra-light, UCI-legal package.

Through advanced in-house development and direct collaboration with world-class riders, we’ve introduced this product at an exceptional value-for-money price compared to alternative high-end track handlebars — without compromising on materials, engineering precision, or overall performance.

Crafted from aerospace-grade Toray carbon fibre with a proprietary high-modulus resin system, this bar strikes the perfect balance between minimal weight and maximum rigidity — ideal for explosive accelerations and sustained power delivery on the boards.

Developed in close partnership with professional riders, the Carbon Aero Bunch Bars have been designed from the inside out to refine body positioning, minimize aerodynamic losses, and amplify race-day performance at the highest level.

CFD-Optimized Aerodynamics

Every curve and contour of the Carbon Aero Bunch Bars have been meticulously CFD-optimized (Computational Fluid Dynamics) to achieve the lowest possible drag without compromising control or comfort.

By simulating thousands of airflow scenarios in a virtual wind tunnel, our engineers refined the handlebar’s shaping to ensure air flows seamlessly around the rider’s hands, arms, and upper body. The result is a bar that doesn’t just look fast — it’s been engineered to save watts when it matters most.

Key aerodynamic benefits include:

Up to 7% Drag Reduction
compared to traditional round-profile handlebars

Minimized Frontal Area
– Narrow tops slice through the air, reducing turbulence and improving efficiency

Optimized Pressure Zones
– Subtle shaping smooths airflow transitions across grip positions, reducing drag hotspots

Aerodynamic Integration
– Designed to work in harmony with natural riding posture, creating a clean, low-drag silhouette without compromising stability

Performance Validated
– CFD insights were verified with on-track testing alongside professional riders to ensure real-world aerodynamic gains

In elite points racing, where average speeds can approach 50 km/h, these aerodynamic advantages translate into measurable watt savings, reduced fatigue, and a competitive edge when it matters most.

Five Versatile Grip Positions

Designed for the demands of modern bunch racing, the Carbon Aero Bunch Bars offers five optimised grip positions to enhance control, comfort, and aerodynamic efficiency:

Classic Drops
– Maximum control with a traditional, confident feel.

Forward Drops
– Slide your hands forward, lower your elbows, and cut your frontal drag for aero gains.

Hood-Grip
– The now-essential “fake hoods” position, providing a raised posture that promotes aerobic recovery — crucial in today’s high-intensity bunch racing.

Pursuit Grip
– Streamlined wrists and forearms align naturally, minimising drag while maintaining a secure, stable hold.

Top Grip
– Aero-profiled flat tops provide a stable platform for Madison slings and controlled upper-body positioning.

Race-Optimised Geometry

The reach and drop are meticulously balanced to deliver aggressive positioning when required, yet remain comfortable and stable during long sessions, breakaways, or high-paced attacks.

Fully UCI-approved for all current and forthcoming regulations (1 January 2027), ensuring unrestricted use at every level of elite competition.

UCI LEGAL -

As of the UCI's 12 June 2025 announcement all our handlebars are still perfectly legal for use in UCI accredited events until 1 January 2027. It is highly unlikely the UCI announcement from 12 June 2025 will be implemented in 2027 as it will even ban the use of children's and women's specific sizes. A meeting of all stakeholders is scheduled to discuss this soon. Please note this announcement also only refers to UCI events such as World Cups, World Championships and Olympic Games. No reciprocal announcements have been made by any governing body to localise the 2027 changes for example British Cycling have not announced a similar change for national level events.
